rules.title: Application screening fee cap ($30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to the actual out-of-pocket cost of gathering applicant information, and never more than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI since January 1, 1998. Unused portions must be returned if no reference check or credit report is obtained.
rules.key_value: Actual cost, max $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted from 1998-01-01)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, for screening residential rental units.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt deposit and fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date reflects the most recent amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); the $30 cap itself predates this amendment, but the document does not state its original effective date.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee if they know or should know that no rental unit is available now or within a reasonable time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and their agents accepting applications for residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date reflects the most recent amendment (AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); the provision may have been in force earlier, which the document does not state.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-qualified-applicant process or full refund to non-selected applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if it either reviews completed applications in order received, approves the first applicant meeting written screening criteria, and charges only applicants actually considered (refunding inadvertent fees within 7 days), or refunds the full fee to every non-selected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and their agents charging application screening fees for residential rental property.

rules.title: Itemized receipt and copy of credit report to applicant
rules.requirement: A landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt for the screening fee and, if a fee was paid, a copy of the consumer credit report within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and their agents who collect an application screening fee for residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date reflects the most recent amendment (AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); earlier versions may have contained similar requirements.
